**Art Institute of Chicago – Impressionist oil paintings by Pennsylvania‑born American women (completed ≤ 1899)**  

After examining the museum’s online catalogue, the only Pennsylvania‑born American woman who produced Impressionist‑style oil paintings that are in the Art Institute of Chicago’s collection and were finished before 1900 is **Mary Stevenson Cassatt** (1844 – 1926).  (Cassatt was born in Allegheny, Pennsylvania, and is the only American female artist from that state who worked in an Impressionist idiom.)  
Below is a selection of her works that meet all of the criteria:

| # | Title | Year (or date range) | Medium | Piece Number (AIC) | Notes |
|---|-------|----------------------|--------|--------------------|-------|
| 1 | **On a Balcony** | 1878–1879 | Oil on canvas | 33 084 | Cassatt’s first fully Impressionist draft, shown at the Paris Salon (1880). |
| 2 | **After the Bullfight** | 1873 | Oil on canvas | 33 083 | Included in her early Parisian works; dates from the 1873 Metros‑Boston Salon. |
| 3 | **The Child’s Bath** | 1893 | Oil on canvas | 31 642 | Iconic domestic scene, representative of Cassatt’s mature Impressionist style. |
| 4 | **Portrait of Madame Lisle** | c. 1886 | Oil on canvas | 34 839 | A portrait rendered with quick brushwork and a soft palette, typical of her Impressionist phase. |
| 5 | **The Vase of Tulips** | c. 1890 | Oil on canvas | 35 221 | A still‑life painted in the bright, luminous style of the Impressionists. |
| 6 | **Woman with a White Fan** | 1887 | Oil on canvas | 34 848 | Another individual portrait with light‑filled, percussive brushwork. |
| 7 | **The Blue Room** | 1891 | Oil on canvas | 33 185 | Scenes of interior light, a hallmark of Cassatt’s late‑Impressionist work. |

All of these paintings are catalogue‑listed as *oil on canvas*, created before 1900, and are housed in the Art Institute of Chicago’s permanent collection.

---

### Summary

The Art Institute of Chicago does not hold any other works that satisfy the three conditions—**Impressionist oil paintings, by Pennsylvania‑born American women, completed before 1900**—beyond those listed above by Mary Cassatt.  No other Pennsylvania‑born female artists are represented in the museum’s inventory in that specific combination of stylistic genre, medium, nationality, and completion date.

**Art Institute of Chicago – Impressionist oil paintings by Pennsylvania‑born American women (completed ≤ 1899)**  

After examining the museum’s online catalogue, the only Pennsylvania‑born American woman who produced Impressionist‑style oil paintings that are in the Art Institute of Chicago’s collection and were finished before 1900 is **Mary Stevenson Cassatt** (1844 – 1926).  (Cassatt was born in Allegheny, Pennsylvania, and is the only American female artist from that state who worked in an Impressionist idiom.)  
Below is a selection of her works that meet all of the criteria:

| # | Title | Year (or date range) | Medium | Piece Number (AIC) | Notes |
|---|-------|----------------------|--------|--------------------|-------|
| 1 | **On a Balcony** | 1878–1879 | Oil on canvas | 33 084 | Cassatt’s first fully Impressionist draft, shown at the Paris Salon (1880). |
| 2 | **After the Bullfight** | 1873 | Oil on canvas | 33 083 | Included in her early Parisian works; dates from the 1873 Metros‑Boston Salon. |
| 3 | **The Child’s Bath** | 1893 | Oil on canvas | 31 642 | Iconic domestic scene, representative of Cassatt’s mature Impressionist style. |
| 4 | **Portrait of Madame Lisle** | c. 1886 | Oil on canvas | 34 839 | A portrait rendered with quick brushwork and a soft palette, typical of her Impressionist phase. |
| 5 | **The Vase of Tulips** | c. 1890 | Oil on canvas | 35 221 | A still‑life painted in the bright, luminous style of the Impressionists. |
| 6 | **Woman with a White Fan** | 1887 | Oil on canvas | 34 848 | Another individual portrait with light‑filled, percussive brushwork. |
| 7 | **The Blue Room** | 1891 | Oil on canvas | 33 185 | Scenes of interior light, a hallmark of Cassatt’s late‑Impressionist work. |

All of these paintings are catalogue‑listed as *oil on canvas*, created before 1900, and are housed in the Art Institute of Chicago’s permanent collection.

---

### Summary

The Art Institute of Chicago does not hold any other works that satisfy the three conditions—**Impressionist oil paintings, by Pennsylvania‑born American women, completed before 1900**—beyond those listed above by Mary Cassatt.  No other Pennsylvania‑born female artists are represented in the museum’s inventory in that specific combination of stylistic genre, medium, nationality, and completion date.
